title: How Did Humans Invent the Clock?
description:
For most of human history, nobody knew exactly what time it was. So how did we get clocks that lose one second in 100 million years?

From shadows on Egyptian obelisks to atomic clocks inside every GPS satellite, this is the story of how humans learned to measure time: a 12-metre Chinese clock tower, a bored Galileo watching a lamp swing, a naval disaster that killed 1,400 sailors, a self-taught carpenter who solved longitude, railways that invented time zones, and the crystal vibrating 32,768 times a second inside your watch.

In this video:
• Why we have 24 hours (and why ancient hours changed length)
• Water clocks, Ctesibius and Su Song's 1088 clock tower
• Galileo, Huygens and the pendulum clock
• The longitude problem and John Harrison's sea watch
• Railway time, time zones and the 'day of two noons'
• Quartz watches, atomic clocks and GPS
